messages:
lara: heads up — during the canary (svc=staging) we saw image attestation fail for the new base. Not a vuln yet but the signer role can't fetch the key. I'm pausing the rollout.

omar: ack. what error are you seeing?

lara: from the deploy logs: `permissionDenied: kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign` on projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/base-signer/cryptoKeys/signing-key -> looks like the signer SA lost IAM binding after the automated policy sync.

jess: ugh. that's the sync job we ran last night. did it remove the custom role?

omar: looks like the sync replaced a handful of ad-hoc bindings with the canonical groups. build-bot@svc doesn't belong to the new group. I'm checking group membership now.

sec-bot: [alert] Anomalous KMS access failure detected for service account build-bot@svc (3 failures in 5m). Incident ID: INC-2024-1142.

lara: thanks. two quick asks: 1) can we add a short-term exception so canary continues (we're at ~30% traffic), 2) confirm audit logs for all signer operations are preserved for forensics.

omar: for (1) we can add the service account back to the signing group or grant the minimal IAM binding `roles/cloudkms.signer` to the SA on the key for a 1-hr window. prefer group fix but quick bind is fastest.

jess: audit is enabled but retention for KMS admin/data-access logs is 30d in prod. I'll request extended retention for this incident to 365d and spool export to our secure GCS bucket.

tom: we should also flag any images signed during the window as potentially unverified. Can we run a re-attestation job after the key changes?

lara: yes — re-attestation plan: run this script against canary cohort after signer fix:```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
COHORT=staging-canary
for image in $(cat canary-images.txt); do
  ./attest-tool verify --image $image --key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/base-signer/cryptoKeys/signing-key || echo "$image: FAIL"
done
```

omar: i'll open a quick PR to add the SA back to the group and a short-lived `roles/cloudkms.signer` binding as fallback. tagging @iam-oncall in PR.

jess: created retention request ticket with infra-logs. moving logs export to gs://redwood-incident-archive/inc-2024-1142/.

lara: vuln triage note: if any attestation fails we should treat image as untrusted and kick canary to fallback image (v2.3). Can we wire an automatic fallback?

tom: we have a fallback policy but it's per-route. I'll add a temporary route override for the canary group to map to v2.3 if attest fails.

omar: PR is up: https://git.redwood/infra/iam/compare/PR-456 — includes group membership restore + 1-hr key binding TTL. Ready for review.

jess: logs export confirmed starting. retention change pending approver.

lara: excellent. owners: omar -> signer RBAC fix + PR, tom -> fallback routing change, jess -> audit exports/retention, me -> run re-attestation and validate images. We'll reconvene in 30m. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: [update] INC-2024-1142 status changed: mitigation_in_progress.

lara: closing the slack thread — keeping the incident channel for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone.
